library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Mukap_2025_amoxicillin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Mukap_2025_amoxicillin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.01491-24>

Mukap 2025 characterised intravenous amoxicillin in neonates treated for
confirmed or suspected sepsis at Port Moresby General Hospital, Papua New
Guinea, and used the model to compare existing and simplified dosing regimens
for the probability of target attainment (fT > MIC) and for the proportion of
neonates with concentrations above 140 mg/L, the neurotoxicity surrogate.

The structural model was fitted to dried-blood-spot (DBS) concentrations from
heel-prick capillary blood. A single venous plasma sample per neonate entered
through an estimated "ratio in plasma to in DBS" (Table 2). The model has two
compartments with first-order elimination; body weight scales all clearance
and volume terms allometrically (reference 2.8 kg, exponents fixed at 0.75 and
1), clearance matures exponentially with postmenstrual age (PMA) and rises by
57% once postnatal age (PNA) exceeds 2 days (Table 2):

`CL = 0.856 * (WT / 2.8)^0.75 * exp(0.0816 * (PMA - 39)) * (1 + 0.57 * [PNA > 2 days])`

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Mukap_2025_amoxicillin")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

rxode2 warns that the interoccasion etas are not mu-referenced; that is
expected for occasion-indexed random effects and does not affect simulation.

The model returns two concentrations: `Cc`, the DBS concentration
(`central / vc`), and `Cc_plasma`, the plasma concentration. As printed in the
paper, `Cc_plasma = 0.783 * Cc` (with interindividual variability on the
ratio). The paper's own paired samples point the other way (plasma higher than
DBS); see [The plasma-to-DBS ratio](#the-plasma-to-dbs-ratio) below before
using `Cc_plasma`.

# Population

177 neonates aged up to 2 months with bacteriologically confirmed (9.0%) or
clinically suspected sepsis were enrolled in a prospective observational study
(Mukap 2025 Table 1). Median weight was 2.8 kg (IQR 2.1-3.3, range 0.9-5.5),
median gestational age 38 weeks (IQR 37-40, range 28-42), median PNA 0 days
(IQR 0-2, range 0-48) and median PMA 273 days (39 weeks; range 196-328 days).
57% of those with recorded sex were male (12 unknown). More than three-quarters
were term babies with early-onset sepsis. Amoxicillin was given as 30 mg/kg
intravenous slow injections over 3 min, twice daily (BD) for the first 7 days
of life and three times daily (TDS) thereafter. DBS samples were collected at
baseline and 0.5, 1, 4, 12, 24 and 48 h after the first dose (1,145 retained)
and one venous plasma sample at about 24 h (134 retained).

```{r population}
str(ui$population)
```

# Source trace

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| CL (per 2.8 kg, PMA 39 weeks, PNA <= 2 days) | 0.856 L/h | Table 2, theta1 |
| Vc (per 2.8 kg) | 4.11 L | Table 2, VC |
| Q (per 2.8 kg) | 0.406 L/h | Table 2, Q |
| Vp (per 2.8 kg) | 1.35 L | Table 2, VP |
| Plasma-to-DBS ratio | 0.783 | Table 2, 'Ratio in plasma to in DBS' |
| Allometric exponents (CL and Q; Vc and Vp) | 0.75; 1 (fixed) | Supplement section 2 |
| PMA maturation, FMAT = exp(theta (PMA - 39)) | theta = 0.0816 /week | Table 2 |
| PNA effect, CL x (1 + theta) when PNA > 2 days | theta = 0.57 | Table 2 |
| IIV CL, Vc, ratio | 49.5%, 42.2%, 47.7% | Table 2 (100 x sqrt(variance), footnote) |
| IOV CL, Vc (each dose an occasion) | 31.8%, 34.6% | Table 2; Supplement section 2 |
| Residual error, log DBS | 0.182 (log-scale SD) | Table 2, AddLnDBS |
| Residual error, log plasma | 0.584 (log-scale SD) | Table 2 row 'PropPlasma', footnote 'AddLnPlasma' |
| Two-compartment structure, first-order elimination | -- | Results, Pharmacokinetic modeling |
| Plasma = ratio x DBS | -- | Methods, Simulations ('adjusted ... by multiplication') |

# Typical-value checks

The Discussion quotes the point clearance estimate as 0.31 L/h/kg, which is
theta1 per 2.8 kg (0.856 / 2.8 = 0.306 L/h/kg) for a neonate at PMA 39 weeks
and PNA up to 2 days.

```{r typical-cl}
cl_per_kg <- 0.856 / 2.8
cl_per_kg
stopifnot(abs(cl_per_kg - 0.31) < 0.005)
```

The typical DBS profile after a single 30 mg/kg dose in a 2.8 kg neonate at
PMA 39 weeks and PNA 0 days is compared with the observed median of the
prediction-corrected VPC (Supplementary Figure S4, digitised by the
maintainers on the natural-log scale: about 2.85 at 0.5 h, 1.9 at 4 h and 1.0
at 12 h after the dose).

```{r typical-profile}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(ui)
ev_typ <- data.frame(
  id = 1L,
  time = c(0, seq(0.25, 12, by = 0.25)),
  evid = c(1L, rep(0L, 48)),
  amt = c(30 * 2.8, rep(0, 48)),
  cmt = "central",
  dvid = c(NA_integer_, rep(1L, 48)),
  WT = 2.8, PAGE = 39, PNA = 0, OCC = 1
)
typ <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_typ, useLinCmt = FALSE))

vpc_median <- data.frame(time = c(0.5, 4, 12), obs_log = c(2.85, 1.9, 1.0)) |>
  mutate(obs_median = exp(obs_log))
typ_check <- vpc_median |>
  left_join(typ |> select(time, Cc), by = "time") |>
  mutate(ratio = Cc / obs_median)
knitr::kable(
  typ_check |>
    select(time, obs_median, Cc, ratio) |>
    rename(
      "Time after dose (h)" = time,
      "Observed VPC median (mg/L)" = obs_median,
      "Typical DBS prediction (mg/L)" = Cc,
      "Predicted / observed" = ratio
    ),
  digits = 2
)
stopifnot(all(typ_check$ratio > 0.6 & typ_check$ratio < 1.6))
```

```{r typical-plot, fig.cap = "Typical DBS concentration after 30 mg/kg in a 2.8 kg neonate (PMA 39 weeks, PNA 0 days) against the observed VPC medians of Supplementary Figure S4."}
ggplot(typ, aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = vpc_median, aes(time, obs_median), colour = "red", size = 2) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "DBS amoxicillin (mg/L)")
```

The prediction-corrected medians sit close to the typical curve, as expected
for a neonate at the cohort median weight and PMA.

# Virtual cohort

The paper simulated 1,000 boys and 1,000 girls per PNA band (< 3 days, 3-7
days, > 7 days) and per PMA week from 33 to 41, with weights from preterm
weight-for-age data that are not reproduced in the paper. Here a smaller
cohort is drawn from the Table 1 marginals instead: PMA normal around 39
weeks (SD 2.15 weeks, matching the 37-40 week IQR; truncated to 28-47) and
weight log-normal around 2.8 kg (log-SD 0.335, matching the 2.1-3.3 kg IQR;
truncated to 0.9-5.5), correlated at an assumed 0.7. Baseline PNA is half
0-2 days, a quarter 3-7 days and a quarter 8-28 days. PNA (in whole days, as
Table 1 reports it) and PMA advance with time on treatment, so the PNA step on
clearance and the PNA-based switch in dosing frequency both happen during the
simulation.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2025)
n_sub <- 200
z1 <- rnorm(n_sub)
z2 <- 0.7 * z1 + sqrt(1 - 0.7^2) * rnorm(n_sub)
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  PMA0 = pmin(pmax(39 + 2.15 * z1, 28), 47),
  WT = pmin(pmax(exp(log(2.8) + 0.335 * z2), 0.9), 5.5),
  PNA0 = sample(c(
    sample(0:2, n_sub / 2, replace = TRUE),
    sample(3:7, n_sub / 4, replace = TRUE),
    sample(8:28, n_sub / 4, replace = TRUE)
  ))
) |>
  mutate(pna_band = cut(PNA0, c(-1, 2, 7, Inf), labels = c("0-2 d", "3-7 d", "> 7 d")))
summary(cohort[, c("PMA0", "WT", "PNA0")])
table(cohort$pna_band)
```

# Dosing regimens

The regimens of the paper's Simulations section and Figure 1. The dosing
interval at each dose is chosen from the neonate's PNA at that time (whole
days): BD while PNA is at or below the cut-off, then the later frequency.

```{r regimens}
regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~mgkg, ~cutoff_d, ~tau_late, ~label,
  "png", 30, 7, 6, "PNG: 30 mg/kg BD to day 7, then QID",
  "who", 50, 7, 8, "WHO: 50 mg/kg BD to day 7, then TDS",
  "meningitis", 100, 7, 8, "Meningitis: 100 mg/kg BD to day 7, then TDS",
  "proposed", 30, 2, 8, "Proposed: 30 mg/kg BD to day 2, then TDS",
  "fixed", NA, 2, 8, "Fixed: 52 mg (< 3 kg) or 104 mg, BD to day 2, then TDS"
)
horizon <- 96

dose_times <- function(pna0, cutoff_d, tau_late, horizon) {
  t <- 0
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (t < horizon) {
    out <- c(out, t)
    t <- t + if (floor(pna0 + t / 24) > cutoff_d) tau_late else 12
  }
  out
}

subject_events <- function(s, reg, horizon, obs_step) {
  dt <- dose_times(s$PNA0, reg$cutoff_d, reg$tau_late, horizon)
  amt <- if (is.na(reg$mgkg)) ifelse(s$WT < 3, 52, 104) else reg$mgkg * s$WT
  obs <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, horizon, by = obs_step), dt + 0.05)))
  d <- rbind(
    data.frame(time = dt, evid = 1L, amt = amt, dvid = NA_integer_),
    data.frame(time = obs, evid = 0L, amt = 0, dvid = 1L)
  )
  d <- d[order(d$time, -d$evid), ]
  # Each dose is an occasion; the model encodes 21.
  d$OCC <- pmin(pmax(findInterval(d$time, dt), 1), 21)
  d$id <- s$id
  d$cmt <- "central"
  d$WT <- s$WT
  d$PAGE <- s$PMA0 + d$time / 168
  # PNA in whole days, converted to months.
  d$PNA <- floor(s$PNA0 + d$time / 24) / 30.4375
  d
}

build_events <- function(cohort, reg, horizon, obs_step = 0.25) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(
    split(cohort, cohort$id), subject_events,
    reg = reg, horizon = horizon, obs_step = obs_step
  ))
}
```

# Neurotoxicity surrogate: replicating Figure 1 B

Figure 1 B reports the percentage of simulated neonates with plasma
concentrations above 140 mg/L: 6.9% for the existing PNG regimen, 24.9% for
the WHO regimen, 84.5% for 100 mg/kg (text), 6.1% for the proposed regimen and
4.1% for fixed-volume dosing. The simulation length and whether residual
error was added are not stated; here the maximum individual prediction over
the first 96 h is used. The same subjects (same random effects) are used for
every regimen. Both readings of the plasma-to-DBS ratio are shown: the
packaged `Cc_plasma` (plasma = 0.783 x DBS) and the alternative
plasma = DBS / 0.783.

```{r neurotox}
sims <- list()
for (k in seq_len(nrow(regimens))) {
  reg <- regimens[k, ]
  ev <- build_events(cohort, reg, horizon)
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250304)
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(ui, ev, useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame"))
  s$regimen <- reg$regimen
  sims[[reg$regimen]] <- s
}
sim_all <- bind_rows(sims)

cmax_sub <- sim_all |>
  group_by(regimen, id) |>
  summarise(
    cmax_dbs = max(Cc),
    cmax_plasma = max(Cc_plasma),
    cmax_plasma_alt = max(Cc / ratio_plasma_central),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
neuro <- cmax_sub |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(
    pct_plasma = 100 * mean(cmax_plasma > 140),
    pct_plasma_alt = 100 * mean(cmax_plasma_alt > 140),
    pct_dbs = 100 * mean(cmax_dbs > 140),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    data.frame(
      regimen = c("png", "who", "meningitis", "proposed", "fixed"),
      published = c(6.9, 24.9, 84.5, 6.1, 4.1)
    ),
    by = "regimen"
  ) |>
  left_join(regimens |> select(regimen, label), by = "regimen") |>
  arrange(match(regimen, regimens$regimen))

knitr::kable(
  neuro |>
    select(label, published, pct_plasma, pct_plasma_alt, pct_dbs) |>
    rename(
      "Regimen" = label,
      "Published (%)" = published,
      "Cc_plasma = 0.783 x DBS (%)" = pct_plasma,
      "Plasma = DBS / 0.783 (%)" = pct_plasma_alt,
      "DBS (%)" = pct_dbs
    ),
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Percentage of neonates with a maximum concentration above 140 mg/L over 96 h. Replicates Figure 1 B of Mukap 2025."
)

# The percentages above are tail counts of 200 subjects and can move by a
# few subjects across rxode2 builds, so the dose ordering is asserted on the
# median maximum concentration instead.
cmax_med <- cmax_sub |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(med = median(cmax_plasma), .groups = "drop")
med <- setNames(cmax_med$med, cmax_med$regimen)
stopifnot(
  med[["meningitis"]] > 1.5 * med[["who"]],
  med[["who"]] > 1.3 * med[["png"]]
)
```

The ordering across regimens is reproduced under both readings. The
magnitudes are not: with the packaged `Cc_plasma` the percentages fall well
below the published ones, while the alternative reading (plasma = DBS / 0.783)
lands close to the published figures for the 30 and 50 mg/kg regimens and the
fixed-volume regimen. The virtual cohort is not the paper's (see above), so
this is supporting rather than conclusive evidence; the next section sets out
why the alternative is the more plausible reading.

# The plasma-to-DBS ratio

Table 2 labels the estimate 0.783 the "Ratio in plasma to in DBS", and the
Methods (Simulations) state that "the simulated DBS concentrations were then
adjusted to free plasma concentrations by multiplication", i.e.
plasma = 0.783 x DBS. That is the relationship the packaged model encodes.

The paper's own data contradict that direction. In the 135 paired samples,
"the amoxicillin concentration ratios between DBS and plasma were 0.48 (95%
CI: 0.11-0.97), closely related to the average haematocrit value of 0.49"
(Results). DBS was lower than plasma in essentially every pair, as expected
for a drug that stays in plasma (DBS approximates whole blood, roughly
plasma x (1 - haematocrit)). A ratio fitted to those data as
plasma = ratio x DBS would have to be above 1. The data-consistent reading of
0.783 is DBS = 0.783 x plasma, i.e. plasma = DBS / 0.783 = 1.28 x DBS. The
neurotoxicity comparison above points the same way.

```{r ratio-plot, fig.cap = "Typical DBS concentration (Cc), the packaged plasma output (Cc_plasma = 0.783 x DBS) and the alternative plasma = DBS / 0.783 after a single 30 mg/kg dose."}
typ |>
  mutate(plasma_alt = Cc / 0.783) |>
  select(time, Cc, Cc_plasma, plasma_alt) |>
  pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "output", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(output = recode(output,
    Cc = "DBS (Cc)",
    Cc_plasma = "Plasma, packaged (0.783 x DBS)",
    plasma_alt = "Plasma, alternative (DBS / 0.783)"
  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc, colour = output)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Amoxicillin (mg/L)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

To use the alternative reading, take `Cc / ratio_plasma_central` from the
simulation output instead of `Cc_plasma`, as the neurotoxicity chunk above
does. Fixed-effect and DBS predictions are the same under both readings.

# Probability of target attainment in neonates aged 3-7 days

The Results state that the existing PNG regimen gave 94% and 75.1% of
neonates aged 3-7 days fT > MIC of at least 70% for MICs of 1 and 4 mg/L, and
the proposed regimen 95.6% and 77.4% (Figure 1 C1 and C3). The paper's 24-hour
window is not specified; the second day of treatment (24-48 h) is used here,
on a separate cohort of 200 neonates with baseline PNA 3-7 days, with plasma
concentrations under both readings.

```{r pta}
cohort_37 <- cohort |>
  mutate(id = id, PNA0 = sample(3:7, n_sub, replace = TRUE))
pta_rows <- list()
for (rg in c("png", "proposed")) {
  reg <- regimens[regimens$regimen == rg, ]
  ev <- build_events(cohort_37, reg, horizon = 48, obs_step = 0.1)
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250305)
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(ui, ev, useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame")) |>
    filter(time >= 24, time <= 48)
  for (mic in c(1, 4)) {
    ft <- s |>
      group_by(id) |>
      summarise(
        ft_plasma = mean(Cc_plasma > mic),
        ft_alt = mean(Cc / ratio_plasma_central > mic),
        .groups = "drop"
      )
    pta_rows[[paste(rg, mic)]] <- data.frame(
      regimen = rg, mic = mic,
      pta_plasma = 100 * mean(ft$ft_plasma >= 0.7),
      pta_alt = 100 * mean(ft$ft_alt >= 0.7)
    )
  }
}
pta <- bind_rows(pta_rows) |>
  left_join(
    data.frame(
      regimen = c("png", "png", "proposed", "proposed"),
      mic = c(1, 4, 1, 4),
      published = c(94, 75.1, 95.6, 77.4)
    ),
    by = c("regimen", "mic")
  )
knitr::kable(
  pta |>
    select(regimen, mic, published, pta_plasma, pta_alt) |>
    rename(
      "Regimen" = regimen,
      "MIC (mg/L)" = mic,
      "Published (%)" = published,
      "Cc_plasma (%)" = pta_plasma,
      "Plasma = DBS / 0.783 (%)" = pta_alt
    ),
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Percentage of neonates aged 3-7 days with fT > MIC of at least 70% on day 2. Compare Figure 1 C1 and C3 of Mukap 2025."
)
stopifnot(
  # Higher MIC can only lower attainment for the same concentrations.
  all(pta$pta_plasma[pta$mic == 4] <= pta$pta_plasma[pta$mic == 1]),
  all(pta$pta_alt[pta$mic == 4] <= pta$pta_alt[pta$mic == 1])
)
```

The paper's PTA figures sit higher than both simulated readings for these
neonates. Their 24-hour window and cohort (PMA 33-41 weeks across preterm
weight-for-age) are not reproducible from the text, so this comparison is
qualitative.

# Stochastic DBS profiles over the study design

DBS concentrations over the first 48 h under the study regimen (30 mg/kg BD),
for the virtual cohort, with the paper's DBS sampling times marked.

```{r vpc, fig.cap = "Simulated DBS concentrations (median and 5th-95th percentiles, individual predictions) under 30 mg/kg BD; vertical lines mark the DBS sampling times (0.5, 1, 4, 12, 24, 48 h)."}
reg_study <- tibble::tibble(regimen = "study", mgkg = 30, cutoff_d = 7, tau_late = 8)
ev_study <- build_events(cohort, reg_study, horizon = 48)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250306)
sim_study <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(ui, ev_study, useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame"))
sim_study |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), p50 = median(Cc), p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(0.5, 1, 4, 12, 24, 48), linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (h)", y = "DBS amoxicillin (mg/L)")
```

# PKNCA validation

Non-compartmental analysis of the simulated DBS concentrations over the first
6 h after the first 30 mg/kg dose (before any second dose in every band), by
PNA band. The paper reports no NCA, so there is no published comparison; the
check is that the half-life is shorter once the PNA step on clearance applies.

```{r nca}
nca_conc <- sim_study |>
  filter(time <= 6, !is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc) |>
  left_join(cohort |> select(id, pna_band, WT), by = "id") |>
  distinct(id, time, .keep_all = TRUE)
nca_dose <- cohort |>
  transmute(id, pna_band, time = 0, amt = 30 * WT)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | pna_band + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | pna_band + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 6,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast", "half.life")) |>
  group_by(pna_band, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)
knitr::kable(
  nca_tab |>
    rename(
      "PNA band" = pna_band,
      "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax,
      "AUC0-6 (mg h/L)" = auclast,
      "t1/2 (h)" = half.life
    ),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Median DBS NCA after the first 30 mg/kg dose, by PNA band."
)

# The PNA step on clearance shortens the half-life in neonates older than
# 2 days; a mis-coded PNA unit or threshold would flatten this contrast.
hl <- setNames(nca_tab$half.life, as.character(nca_tab$pna_band))
stopifnot(hl[["3-7 d"]] < hl[["0-2 d"]])
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Plasma-to-DBS ratio direction.** `Cc_plasma = ratio x Cc` follows the
  Table 2 label and the Methods wording. The paper's paired samples (DBS /
  plasma 0.48) and haematocrit physiology indicate DBS = ratio x plasma
  instead, and that reading reproduces the published neurotoxicity
  percentages much more closely (see above). The maintainers kept the printed
  relationship; `Cc / ratio_plasma_central` gives the alternative.
* **PNA threshold.** The Table 2 equation (CL x 1.57 for PNA > 2 days) is
  encoded; the Results prose says "> 3 days old". PNA is supplied in months
  (register convention) and compared against 2 / 30.4375 months.
* **PNA coefficient.** The point estimate 0.57 is encoded. The bootstrap
  median in Table 2, 0.254 (95% CI 0.192-0.379), excludes it; the paper does
  not comment.
* **Residual error.** Both residual errors are additive on the log scale
  (`lnorm`), per the Supplement ("additive error for the log-transformed
  data") and the Table 2 footnote, which defines AddLnPlasma although the
  table row reads PropPlasma.
* **Variability scale.** Table 2 reports variability as 100 x sqrt(variance);
  variances are the squared fractions.
* **Interoccasion variability.** Each dose is an occasion (Supplement). The
  number of occasions is not reported; 21 are encoded (7 days of 8-hourly
  dosing), all sharing one variance per parameter. Records with `OCC` outside
  1-21 carry no IOV.
* **Interindividual variability on the ratio** is assumed log-normal
  (exponential), like the other random effects.
* **PMA units.** PMA is carried in weeks (`PAGE`, declared in weeks for this
  model) because the maturation term is centred on 39 weeks.
* **Virtual cohort.** Drawn from the Table 1 marginals with an assumed
  weight-PMA correlation of 0.7, not from the paper's PMA-week by PNA-band
  grid with preterm weight-for-age data. Simulation length (96 h), the use of
  individual predictions without residual error, and the 24-48 h PTA window
  are the maintainers' choices; the paper does not state them.
